anchor.source: tmp/br2watch/m6/pl_audit.json via the WW-3a sidecar (GL-17: read, not derived)

rule.discriminator: local gradient magnitude on Rec.709 luma (np.gradient Sobel-equivalent); the subject is hard-edged textured mesh, the smoke bed / prop shadow / bloom are SMOOTH washes
rule.edge_rule: an edge row/column is the first/last carrying a contiguous run of >= 3 columns at G >= 15
rule.why_not_the_WW3B_flank_median_rule: the still carries a strong left-right smoke/shadow luminance gradient (flank medians 127-129 L left vs 110-113 L right on the same rows), so a flank-median reference classifies smooth shadow as subject. Demonstrated: it reported a 26-column DARK run at y505-513 x961-986 where the gradient instrument reads G_max 4.72 (smooth). The flank rule was run, printed and DISCARDED with the evidence shown.

man_tight.label: MAN body silhouette (TIGHT — number of record)

vm_all.label: VISUAL MASS: mesh + weapon FX + smoke bed

number_of_record.bracket: TIGHT body silhouette; weapon geometry, VFX, trail and smoke EXCLUDED per GD convention

crown_to_anchor_band.definition: h_px = machine-audited anchor row - adjudicated crown row; the SAME quantity the WW-3B cell reported as its supporting band

ground_contact.reason: the channel_fx smoke bed occludes the ground plane and the feet; the legs fade progressively into it rather than terminating at an edge. Inside the bed the floor diamond texture is fully obliterated (G_max 4.66 vs 24.41 on bare floor).

pale_smudge_below_is_smoke_not_body.evidence: L 128.2 sd 9.4, BRIGHTER than the local bed (125.0 / 117.9) with matching chromaticity; body patches read sd 25-39 and DARKER

harness_cross_check.fraction_is_resolution_invariant_because: KEEP_HEIGHT vertical fov and an identical 16:9 aspect (1600/900 == 1920/1080); the FRACTION carries across, the px number does not
harness_cross_check.box_was_not_tuned_to_match: the rule and both edges were fixed from the calibration before the comparison was computed

composition_facts.convention: offsets are (dx,dy) px against the MEASURED 1920x1080 frame; +y is DOWN-screen. mask centroid = centroid of classified pixels; bbox centre = centre of the bounding box. Both reported because they disagree wherever the mass is lopsided. PIXEL FACTS ONLY — no adjudication of whether the composition reads correctly (R-CPB-17b: the eye rules).

F1_mesh_rides_high_of_anchor.note: the vertical ride of the man+hammer centroid (7.09% of frame height) EXCEEDS the entire body register (6.574%)

F2_mesh_also_rides_left.note: the flag named the vertical asymmetry; the horizontal one is the same size class and was not named

F4_only_the_smoke_bed_is_anchor_centred.note: the largest single visual mass attributable to the subject is a ground-plane FX disc centred on the subject own root; it is what fixes the composition to the anchor while the geometry does not

ambiguities.q: the artifact is 1920x1080; its filename, its sidecar, ledger row WW-3a and the charter all say 1600x900
ambiguities.disposition: DECLARED, NOT RESOLVED — ROUTED UP. Four instruments agree on the bytes (PIL, sips, ffprobe, raw PNG IHDR at offset 16 = 00 00 07 80 / 00 00 04 38). sha and byte count MATCH the charter exactly: right artifact, wrong label. Measurement proceeded because the charter HALT condition is the sha (PASS) and the defect is bounded: aspect is identical (1.7778) and the fov is VERTICAL under KEEP_HEIGHT, so every screen-HEIGHT FRACTION is resolution-invariant. All fractions stand; pixel counts are stated at 1080 and restated at the 900 convention where a WW-3B comparable exists. What it DOES break: the harness stated 188.07 px, and the ledger 495.83 anchor row, which for these bytes is 595.00. Whether the render was always 1080 or a later step resampled is a harness question, not diagnosed here.

ambiguities.q: crown 516 vs the literal WW-3B >=3-column-at-28L rule, which would give 522
ambiguities.disposition: BOTH REPORTED, NOT AVERAGED. The horn is a two-pixel-wide taper; a 3-column rule under-reads thin tapers by construction. Adopted G>=15 run>=3 (corroborated by eye at 18x) -> 516 -> 6.5741%. Literal WW-3B rule -> 522 -> 6.0185%. First onset -> 515 -> 6.6667%. Band 6.019-6.667%.

ambiguities.q: the harness projection and this still are different ticks
ambiguities.disposition: DECLARED, UNRESOLVABLE HERE. The sidecar reads the subject AABB at the shot FIRST tick (1570); this still is tick 1635.333. Largest named suspect for the 8.95 pp cross-check gap, and NOT sized — no still of tick 1570 exists in this cell reach.

ambiguities.q: the pale smudge below the legs, y599-608 — foot or smoke?
ambiguities.disposition: EXCLUDED, test shown. BRIGHTER than surround (L 128.2 vs 125.0 / 117.9) where body is DARKER; SMOOTH (sd 9.4) where body is structured (sd 25-39); chromaticity matches the bed to under 0.01 per channel fraction. Had it been admitted as a foot, bottom 608 and TIGHT 8.5185%.

ambiguities.q: is the helm horn part of the body silhouette?
ambiguities.disposition: INCLUDED per GD silhouette convention (worn geometry counts; VFX does not). Noted that the harness own drawn-height basis explicitly EXCLUDES horns and weapon. The alternative reading — top of the helm dome — was attempted and ABANDONED as dishonest: at this scale the dome cannot be separated from the gripping gauntlets and the haft lower end. No number offered for it.

ambiguities.q: bloom edges are structure-positive (G max 54.57) and annex x967-999 into the mesh mask
ambiguities.disposition: HANDLED BY ENVELOPE, DECLARED. Hammer band cut at x>960. The gap was verified before it was used: at y468-480 mesh columns run 900-946, nothing from ~947 to ~966, resume at 967.

ambiguities.q: the hammer left edge abuts a cast member at x~899
ambiguities.disposition: REPORTED AT 900, CONTESTED. Structure is CONTINUOUS x886-949 — structure alone cannot part them. Luminance puts the seam at x~899 (x890-898 read L 45-95, x900-902 read L 118-166). If the hammer is BEHIND the neighbour its true left extent is occluded and unmeasurable. Affects w_px of the man+hammer and generous boxes ONLY; every h_frac untouched.

ambiguities.q: threshold sensitivity of the adopted rule
ambiguities.disposition: MEASURED AND PRINTED. Sweep G>=14/17/20/24/28 at run>=3 gives bottoms 587/582/581/581/572 and horn-band crowns 516 at T=14, 527-528 at T>=17 (the same thin-taper effect as A1). STATED TOLERANCE on the number of record: +/-3 px bottom, +/-6 px crown -> h_frac 6.019-6.667%.

ambiguities.q: the gradient responds ON the boundary, so edges may sit ~1 px outside every extreme reported
ambiguities.disposition: DECLARED, NOT CORRECTED. Systematic, same sign on all four edges, ~+/-1 px. Compensating would be a preference dressed as a measurement.

negative_results: N1. gp_seg.py NOT run. Its colour-distance seeding cannot separate an armoured figure from a smoke-washed floor of near-identical chromaticity (subject r/g/b frac 0.334-0.341 / 0.32-0.33 / 0.333-0.345 against bed 0.330 / 0.321 / 0.350). Skipped deliberately rather than run for the look of it. Same call as WW-3B, opposite reason: there warm-on-warm, here neutral-on-neutral.

N2. Chromaticity FAILED as a discriminator and the failure is informative: the smoke bed neutralises everything it covers, subject and bed differing by under 0.01 in every channel fraction. That is why this cell is built on STRUCTURE instead; the calibration is printed so the substitution is auditable.

N3. The WW-3B flank-median rule produced a CONFIDENT FALSE POSITIVE — a 26-column DARK run at y505-513 / x961-986 which is smooth shadow (G max 4.72). Kept on the record at evidence/DISCARDED-flankmedian-rows-{player,upper}.txt rather than deleted.

N4. The arc tail could not be followed past y634: below it the warm mask fires on a cast member tan armour at x1022-1043 / y641-672, a component SEPARATE from the arc (gap y635-640). Had those been admitted the generous box would read 19.8% and landed within 1.1 pp of the harness 20.896% for spurious reasons. Named so the near-coincidence cannot later be quoted as agreement.
cannot_answer: The ground-contact row. Not measurable on this still at all — the smoke bed occludes the ground plane and the feet, and the legs fade rather than terminate. Bracketed [587,599]; the anchor row 595.00 falls inside the bracket.
Whether the subject register would match at tick 1570, the tick the harness projected. No still of that tick exists in this cell reach.
Whether the 1600x900 / 1920x1080 divergence is a render-argument defect or a later resample. Harness question, routed, not diagnosed.
Whether this frame reads as GD-family beside BR2W. Out of seam; the eye rules (R-CPB-17b).
confound_DECLARED: Subject-height fraction conflates CAMERA FRAMING with BODY SIZE, and every row in the context table photographs a DIFFERENT BODY: a Grim Dawn human, a Grim Dawn werewolf, our werewolf at x1.29 parity, and now a 1.71 m armoured man carrying a hammer scaled 1.95. A difference in h_frac does not by itself establish that two cameras differ, and equality would not establish that they match. Here the cameras are IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION — WW-3a pinned the offset to 0.000000000000 m and the anchor to sub-millipixel — so every difference in the table is body, pose, weapon scale and tick. Nothing in it is lens.
headline: The prediction on ledger row WW-3a was that the subject would OVER-READ against the 12.96% canon-boom band, and 20.896% was reported as that over-read arriving. On the pixels the fighter BODY UNDER-READS EVERYTHING: 0.934x GD human form, 0.665x the ratified BR2W werewolf, 0.445x a GD werewolf. Only when the oversized hammer and then its trail are annexed does the figure climb past BR2W. The over-read is real but it lives in the WEAPON AND ITS FX, not in the man.
